Class StaticDelegation

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.python.processing.staticcompile.StaticDelegation
@Internal public final class StaticDelegation extends Object
Whether the Python callers of a compiled method may run its Java body, and how the rewritten Python method guards the call (see apply_delegation). A Python caller must see what the Python body would give it:
  • every argument must reach the Java parameter unchanged: an int in the range of the Java integer, a float, a bool, a str, or None for a boxed parameter, each of exactly that type (a bool is no int, an int is no float here), or a Java object of the parameter's class, which the boundary hands over as itself, checked on every call;
  • a body without side effects (no write to self, no Java call) runs the Python body instead when the Java body fails, so an int that outgrows a long, which Java raises on and Python promotes, gives Python's result, and any other failure Python's exception. Reading a property of self still counts as without side effects although it goes through getMember and so can run a Python @property getter: when the Java body fails and the Python body runs, such a getter runs twice;
  • a body with side effects cannot be run again: it delegates only when it has no operation that Java raises on where Python promotes, and the failures Python raises as exceptions of its own (a division by zero, an assertion, + on None) reach the caller as those exceptions;
  • the Java exception of a Python exception class reaches the caller as the Python exception it carries when it can only come from the compilation, as it is when it can only have crossed Java code, and a body where it may be either keeps the Python body (see Ir.ExceptionCrossing).
Any other compiled method keeps the Python body for Python callers; Java callers run the Java body all the same.
Since:
5.3.0
Author:
Graeme Rocher

    The conversion a Python caller of a delegated body applies to the collection the body returns: #list, #set or #dict when every return builds a new collection, which the Python body returns as a new Python one; an empty string when the return type is not a collection or every return is a Java object, which the Python body returns as it is; or null when a return may be a collection the Python caller would receive as the same Python object (an attribute, a parameter, a local), which a Java body cannot give back: such a body is not delegated.

  • Method Details

    • target

      public static @Nullable String target(Ir.CompiledBody body)
      The delegation target of a compiled body, as apply_delegation reads it: Class#method#owner=<generated class>#kinds=<kind,...>#retry (or #once for a body that is not run again), or null when its Python callers keep the Python body. #python-exceptions is appended when the rewritten function raises the Python exception a Java exception of the body carries (see Ir.ExceptionCrossing.TRANSLATED). A static method, or a module-level function with an empty class part, names the generated class whose static Java method it calls: Class#method#static=<generated class>#kinds=<kind,...>#retry, or #once for a body with side effects, whose failures reach the Python caller as Python's exceptions through the context the caller entered.
      Parameters:
      body - The compiled body
      Returns:
      The target, or null
